newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland to ask for new bids for Ruch kiosk chain.
newsitem.headline: Poland to ask for new bids for Ruch kiosk chain.

text.p: The Polish treasury ministry said on Wednesday it will invite new bids for the Ruch SA newsstand chain after a consortium led by French Hachette failed to improve its offer.
The announcement paves the way for a domestic consortium led by Universal to bid for the chain which owns 17,000 kiosks nationwide and controls 65 percent of Poland's press distribution market.
"The treasury minister has decided to abandon the negotiations (with Hachette) and announce a new invitation to negotiations," the ministry said in a statement.

Hachette, which had signed an initial agreement with the treasury ministry late last year on buying a 75 percent stake in Ruch, has threatened unspecified action against the Polish government if it breaks the deal.
Earlier this month Treasury Minister Miroslaw Pietrewicz gave the Hachette-led consortium a March 18 deadline to improve its offer.
"The potential investor, Hachette Distribution Service-Wydawcy Prasy, has not improved the important elements of its offer," Wednesday's statement said.
Hachette officials were not immediately available for comment.
Universal spokeswoman Agnieszka Szostek told Reuters on Wednesday that the consortium led by her company would place an offer if a new invitation for bids was announced.
Analysts have said the move could significantly delay the privatisation of Ruch, which needed substantial investment.
"We need privatisation as quickly as possible," Ruch president Alfred Nowak told public television late on Tuesday.
Pietrewicz has said he is keen to protect the treasury's interests and that the accord with Hachette's consortium, also grouping several Polish press firms, was not legally binding.
He said the Universal group's offer was about twice as big.
The group offered to pay $80 million for a 40-percent stake in Ruch and invest a total of $200 million.
